Section 4 UAS Measurement Accuracy Evaluation

In this section, we’ll mask the point cloud detected trees using the slash pile detections to get our final UAS point cloud-derived forest inventory tree list. Then we’ll bring in field-measured data to evaluate our tree detection accuracy. This accuracy evaluation will yield detection accuracy metric including precision, recall (i.e. detection rate), and F-score (overall accuracy or balanced accuracy). Precision is a measure of the proportion of trees that estimated by the UAS method that were actually trees. Recall is a measure of the proportion of field-measured trees that the UAS method correctly identified. The F-score balances precision and recall to create an overall accuracy measure. All of these metrics range between 0 and 1 with values close to one indicating higher tree detection accuracies. In open canopy ponderosa pine forests, tree detection rates generally range from 65-85% (Creasey et al. 2021; Swayze and Tinkham 2023; Tinkham and Woolsey 2024) with higher proportions of larger trees (e.g. 75-95%) being detected compared to smaller tree detection rates (55-75%). As far as I know there has not been a detailed accuracy evaluation of tree detection methods from aerial point cloud data in Pinyon-Juniper forests.

4.1 Remove Slash Piles from Predictions

read back in the tree point data and attach to treatment units

# treetops_fnm
treetops_sf <- sf::st_read(dsn = treetops_fnm, quiet = TRUE)
# attach to treatment unit
treetops_sf <- treetops_sf %>% 
  dplyr::inner_join(
    treetops_sf %>% 
      sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(stand_boundary)) %>% 
      sf::st_intersection(
        stand_boundary %>%
          dplyr::select(unit,block,tretmnt,unit_area_ha) %>% 
          dplyr::rename(type = tretmnt) %>% 
          dplyr::mutate(
            type =
              tolower(type) %>% 
              stringr::str_squish()
          ) %>% 
          dplyr::rename_with(.fn = ~paste0("trtmnt_", .x, recycle0 = T))
      ) %>% 
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      dplyr::select(treeID, tidyselect::starts_with("trtmnt_")) %>% 
      dplyr::group_by(treeID) %>% 
      dplyr::slice(1) %>% 
      dplyr::ungroup()
    , by = "treeID"
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    is_in_trtmnt_unit = ifelse(is.na(trtmnt_type) | trtmnt_type=="control",F,T)
    , dplyr::across(c(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit),ordered)
  )
# treetops_sf %>% dplyr::glimpse()

use our slash pile mask to remove detected “trees” that are likely not trees. if a tree top point falls within the boundary of a detected pile footprint, it will be removed

# save nrow
nrow_temp <- nrow(treetops_sf)
treetops_sf <- 
  sf::st_filter(
    treetops_sf
    , piles_workflow_ans %>% 
      dplyr::filter(is_in_trtmnt_unit, inrange_th_votes>=5) %>% 
      sf::st_union()
    , .predicate = sf::st_disjoint
  )

4.2 Additional UAS-tree Filters

nice. now we’ll keep only trees that are at least 2 m in height since we included trees as small as 1.37 m in our tree detection. This 2 m height sets the lower limit of what is considered a “tree” and if there are field-measured trees that are below this height in the validation data, we’ll apply the same threshold limit. Setting a minimum height threshold will help us remove predictions that are actually shrubs which we know are present with a retention proportion prescribed:

  1. Remove 70% of all woody shrubs (i.e. gambel oak and serviceberry); retain all gambel oak stems greater than 3 inches in basal diameter.
min_tree_ht_m <- 2
treetops_sf <- treetops_sf %>% dplyr::filter(tree_height_m>=min_tree_ht_m)

now, we’ll read in the UAS-delineated tree crown polygons as well so we have them for visualization and get the crown diameter for each tree as the greatest distance across the UAS-delineated crown polygon

we’ll also add a flag for a prediction of if the tree is dead or not based on the RGB spectral classification workflow we described for slash pile identification

dead-tree classification is important for our UAS tree detection validation because these dead trees were not measured during field data collection. Thus, if we did not remove them from our UAS predictions, they would be incorrectly counted as false positive predictions and artificially reduce the UAS tree detection accuracy metrics. Classifying dead trees is also important for quantifying the spatial tree arrangement treatment outcomes since the prescription specifically excludes dead trees from spacing guideline implementation:

  1. Cut all dead pinyon trees <8 inches in basal diameter. Leave all other standing dead trees for wildlife snags. Dead trees are not considered when applying the spacing guides above.
# ```{r,eval=T,purl=FALSE}
# function to clean geometry collections
clean_geometry_collections <- function(df, target_type = "POLYGON") {
  # any?
  geom_types <- as.character(sf::st_geometry_type(df))
  has_gc <- any(geom_types == "GEOMETRYCOLLECTION")
  
  # orig
  if (!has_gc) {
    return(df)
  }
  
  # temp id
  df_temp <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(temp_orig_row_id = dplyr::row_number())
  
  # split the data
  gc_df <- df_temp %>% dplyr::filter(as.character(sf::st_geometry_type(df_temp)) == "GEOMETRYCOLLECTION")
  good_df <- df_temp %>% dplyr::filter(as.character(sf::st_geometry_type(df_temp)) != "GEOMETRYCOLLECTION")
  
  # get only the type and make it a "multi" geom
  gc_multi_df <- 
    gc_df %>%
    sf::st_collection_extract(type = target_type) %>%
    dplyr::select(temp_orig_row_id) %>% 
    dplyr::group_by(temp_orig_row_id) %>%
    # collapse into a single multi-part geometry
    dplyr::summarise(.groups = "drop")
  
  # combine
  final_df <- 
    good_df %>% 
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      gc_multi_df %>% 
        dplyr::inner_join(
          gc_df %>% 
            sf::st_drop_geometry()
          , by = "temp_orig_row_id"
        )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(temp_orig_row_id) %>%
    dplyr::select(-temp_orig_row_id)
  
  return(final_df)
}
# read crowns and get crown measurements
crowns_sf <-
  cloud2trees:::search_dir_final_detected(dir = c2t_process_dir)[["crowns_flist"]] %>% 
  purrr::map(function(x){
    # read it
    crowns_sf_temp <- sf::st_read(
      dsn = x, quiet = TRUE
      , query = 
        sprintf(
          "SELECT * FROM %s WHERE treeID IN (%s)"
          , basename(x) %>% stringr::str_remove("^.*/") %>% stringr::str_remove("\\.[^.]+$")
          , stringr::str_c("'", unique(treetops_sf$treeID), "'", collapse = ", ")
        )
    ) %>% 
    # throw in hey_xxxxxxxxxx to test it works if we include non-existant columns
    dplyr::select( dplyr::any_of(c(
      "hey_xxxxxxxxxx"
      , "treeID"
      , "crown_area_m2"
      , "crown_diameter_m"
      , "inrange_th_votes"
      , "tree_height_m"
      , "tree_x"
      , "tree_y"
    )))
    # check if cols exist
    has_cols <- all(c("crown_area_m2", "crown_diameter_m") %in% names(crowns_sf_temp))
    
    if(!has_cols){
      # get the crown data
      crowns_sf_temp <- 
        crowns_sf_temp %>%
        clean_geometry_collections(target_type = "POLYGON") %>% 
        sf::st_make_valid() %>% 
        cloud2trees::simplify_multipolygon_crowns() %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(
          crown_area_m2 = sf::st_area(.) %>% as.numeric()
        ) %>% 
        cloud2trees:::st_calculate_diameter() %>% 
        dplyr::rename(crown_diameter_m=diameter_m)
      #write....FYI: this replaces the raw data from cloud2trees and excludes trees outside of the treatment units...
      sf::st_write(obj=crowns_sf_temp, dsn = x, quiet = T, append = F)
    }
    
    
    # check if spectral cols exist
    has_cols <- all(c("inrange_th_votes") %in% names(crowns_sf_temp))
    
    if(!has_cols){
      # get the crown data
      # check for spectral
        crowns_sf_spectral_temp <- 
          cloud2trees:::piles_spectral_filter(
            sf_data = crowns_sf_temp
            , rgb_rast = rgb_rast
            # define the band index
            , red_band_idx = 1
            , green_band_idx = 2 
            , blue_band_idx = 3
            # return unfiltered or filtered
            , filter_return = F
          )
        crowns_sf_spectral_temp <- crowns_sf_spectral_temp[["segs_sf"]]
        
        crowns_sf_temp <- 
          crowns_sf_temp %>% 
          dplyr::left_join(
            crowns_sf_spectral_temp %>% 
              sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
              dplyr::select(treeID, inrange_th_votes)
            , by = "treeID"
          )
          
      #write....FYI: this replaces the raw data from cloud2trees and excludes trees outside of the treatment units...
      sf::st_write(obj=crowns_sf_temp, dsn = x, quiet = T, append = F)
    }
    
    
    # return data
    crowns_sf_temp <- crowns_sf_temp %>% 
      dplyr::select(
        treeID
        , crown_area_m2
        , crown_diameter_m
        , inrange_th_votes
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::inner_join(
        treetops_sf %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        # throw in hey_xxxxxxxxxx to test it works if we include non-existant columns
        dplyr::select( -dplyr::any_of(c(
          "hey_xxxxxxxxxx"
          , "crown_area_m2"
          , "crown_diameter_m"
          , "inrange_th_votes"
        )))
        , by = "treeID"
      )
    return(crowns_sf_temp)
    
  }) %>% 
  purrr::list_rbind()

based on the spectral information within the crown footprint, let’s determine a criteria to flag a tree as “dead” based on the inrange_th_votes variable which tells us how many of the 6 spectral index thresholds were met to distinguish a dead wood from living biomass. Where, a value of 5-6 represents high likelihood that the object is not living vegetation (e.g. piled slash) and 1-2 indicates a high likelihood that the object is living vegetation (e.g. small tree/shrub)

what is the distribution of this multi-index spectral threshold voting system?

to be conservative with what we classify as a dead tree, we’ll use the highest level of the inrange_th_votes of “6” which means that all 6 spectral indices agree that the object detected is not living vegetation.

crowns_sf <- crowns_sf %>% dplyr::filter(dplyr::coalesce(inrange_th_votes,0)<=max_inrange_th_votes)

4.3 Reference Field Data

Field-measured data is frequently cited as the gold standard for validating remote sensing methods, but it may be more appropriate to frame field data as the status-quo baseline against which new methodologies are compared. Field inventories carry well-documented challenges, including measurement error, subjective assessments, and data transcription errors (Elzinga et al. 2005; Westfall and Woodall 2007; Luoma et al. 2017; Wang et al. 2019; Sparks et al. 2024). This means that a comparison of the remote sensing forest measurement method against field data evaluates alignment with current operational practices rather than absolute environmental reality. Here are the notes I got along with the field inventory data:

Attached is a csv of the PJ data from the Dawson Creek site. I added the plot center locations and calculated locations of each measured tree from the original distance and azimuth information. Below is a list of notes (and unfortunately some weird things) about it.

  • There are 65 rows (out of 1603) with any missing data. The missing parts are usually in a location-related column with several in a tree metric column.
  • There are 43 DRC (diameter at root collar) observations with two separate values separated by a comma.
  • There are 8 circumstances where there are potential duplicate trees - where plot, distance, and azimuth are identical, but tree information is different.
  • In the metadata crown length is described as “length from first longest side of the adult tree canopy, in m” and crown width is described as “width from second longest side of the adult tree canopy, in m”. However, crown width is frequently greater than the length value and after some looking the length value doesn’t seem to equal height-cbh either.
  • The plot column includes unit, treatment type, and plot ID whereas the tree_id column includes that information as well as a per-plot ID of each tree.

The multiple DRC values are due to multiple stems splitting at ground level. I think we should treat these as one tree, as they’re recorded in the data. To combine the two stem values into a single DRC, we could either take the larger of the two or sum them.

The location duplication issue is due to two trees (or more likely stems from the same individual that split below ground) growing very close together. We should continue to treat them as separate trees, as shown in the data.

Height, cbh, length and width are all in meters. DRC is in cm.

Chojnacky & Rogers (1999) provide information on converting DRC to DBH if needed

let’s get to it and load in the field-measured “truth” data

validation_trees <-
  readr::read_csv("../data/pj_trees_george.csv", show_col_types = F, progress = F) %>% 
  dplyr::rename_with(tolower) %>% 
  dplyr::rename_with(stringr::str_squish) %>% 
  dplyr::rename_with(make.names) %>% 
  dplyr::rename_with(~stringr::str_replace_all(.x, "\\.{2,}", ".")) %>% 
  dplyr::rename_with(~stringr::str_remove(.x, "\\.$")) %>% 
  dplyr::rename_with(~stringr::str_replace_all(.x, "\\.", "_")) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      -c(plot,tree_id,species,unit,treatment_code,drc)
      , as.numeric
    )
    , dplyr::across(
      c(species,unit,treatment_code)
      , ~ stringr::str_trim(.x) %>% toupper()
    )
  ) %>% 
  # clean the DRC
  dplyr::mutate(
    drc = stringr::str_remove_all(drc, " ")
     # split by comma
    , drc_list = stringr::str_split(drc, ",") %>% 
      purrr::map(as.numeric)
    , drc_count = purrr::map_dbl(drc_list, length)
    , drc_max_cm = purrr::map_dbl(drc_list, max)
    , drc_sum_cm = purrr::map_dbl(drc_list, sum)
  ) %>% 
  # dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(drc,",")) %>% dplyr::select(tidyselect::starts_with("drc")) %>% View()
  dplyr::select(-drc_list) %>% 
  # rename
  dplyr::rename_with(
    .cols = c(height,cbh,crown_width,crown_length)
    , .fn = ~paste0(.x,"_m",recycle0 = T)
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::rename_with(
    .cols = c(drc)
    , .fn = ~paste0(.x,"_cm",recycle0 = T)
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Chojnacky & Rogers ([1999](https://doi.org/10.1093/wjaf/14.1.14))
    dbh_cm = dplyr::case_when(
      # the correct code for Juniperus scopulorum is JUSC2...
      species %in% c("JUOS","JUSC","JUSC2") ~ -6.8180 + 1.0222*drc_max_cm + 1.8879*ifelse(drc_count==1,1,0)
      , species == "PIED" ~ -6.8180 + 1.0222*drc_max_cm + 1.8879*ifelse(drc_count==1,1,0) + 1.8971 -0.03998*drc_max_cm
      , species == "QUGA" ~ -6.8180 + 1.0222*drc_max_cm + 1.8879*ifelse(drc_count==1,1,0) + 3.1100 -0.0689*drc_max_cm
      , T ~ NA
    )
  )

validation_trees %>% 
  dplyr::select(height_m, drc_max_cm, dbh_cm, cbh_m) %>%

it looks like the Chojnacky & Rogers (1999) DRC-to-DBH conversion worked well. Those crown and CBH measurements are suspect.

we’ll also use the horizontal crown length and width to evaluate the UAS prediction of canopy cover on a plot-level basis. this canopy cover evaluation will:

  • average the field measured horizontal crown length and width to approximate a circular diameter (Williams et al. 2020)
  • use the diameter to calculate a 2D circular crown area for each field tree
  • calculate the proportion of each plot covered by these assumed circular crowns
  • for each plot, compare this proportion to the proportion of the plot predicted to be covered by crowns of UAS trees whose tree top point falls within the plot. requiring the tree top point to fall within the plot prior to calculating crown cover mimics the field technique of only measuring stems within a plot.

the caveats attached to this approach are that it is notoriously difficult to measure crown dimensions using field techniques (source 2011) and the simple circular shape assumption does not match real-world conditions of irregular crown morphologies…

let’s check out the horizontal crown length and width dimensions measured in the field

  summary() %>%

3rd Qu.: 3.900 3rd Qu.: 4.10

ok, let’s verify those notes we got with the data and look for missing coordinates

validation_trees %>% 
  dplyr::filter(
    is.na(tree_x) | is.na(tree_y)
    | as.character(tree_x)=="" | as.character(tree_y)==""
  ) %>%
  nrow() %>% 
  stringr::str_c(" trees are missing location data")
## [1] "61 trees are missing location data"

we’ll exclude these trees from the accuracy evaluation since we need location data to perform a spatial instance segmentation analysis

let’s check out how many trees are missing height measurement data which we will use for matching with our UAS predicted trees

validation_trees %>% 
  dplyr::filter(
    is.na(height_m)
  ) %>%
  nrow() %>% 
  stringr::str_c(" trees are missing height data")
## [1] "4 trees are missing height data"

we’ll exclude these as well and implement the exclusions using a spatial join with the treatment unit boundaries. we’ll also set a minimum tree height threshold of 2 m to define what is considered a “tree”. a minimum tree height of 2 m will be used to filter the reference field trees which we also applied to our UAS-detected trees.

# sort(validation_trees$crown_length_m, decreasing = T) %>% head()
# sort(validation_trees$crown_width_m, decreasing = T) %>% head()
# drop missings and spatial it
validation_trees <- 
  validation_trees %>% 
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(plot)
    , stringr::str_trim(plot)!=""
    , !is.na(plot_center_x)
    , !is.na(plot_center_y)
    , !is.na(tree_x)
    , !is.na(tree_y)
    , !is.na(height_m)
    , height_m>=min_tree_ht_m
  ) %>%  
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      c(crown_length_m, crown_width_m)
      , ~ ifelse(.x>100,.x/100,.x)
    )
    # do it again for really bad ones
    , dplyr::across(
      c(crown_length_m, crown_width_m)
      , ~ ifelse(.x>10,.x/10,.x)
    )
    , crown_diam_m = dplyr::case_when(
      !is.na(crown_length_m) & !is.na(crown_width_m) ~ (crown_length_m+crown_width_m)/2
      , !is.na(crown_width_m) ~ crown_width_m
      , !is.na(crown_length_m) ~ crown_length_m
      , T ~ as.numeric(NA)
    )
  ) %>% 
  # guessing this is WGS 84
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("tree_x", "tree_y"), crs = 4326, remove = F) %>% 
  sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(stand_boundary))
# attach to treatment unit
validation_trees <-
  validation_trees %>% 
  dplyr::inner_join(
     validation_trees %>% 
      sf::st_intersection(
        stand_boundary %>%
          dplyr::select(unit,block,tretmnt,unit_area_ha) %>% 
          dplyr::rename(type = tretmnt) %>% 
          dplyr::mutate(
            type =
              tolower(type) %>% 
              stringr::str_squish()
          ) %>% 
          dplyr::rename_with(.fn = ~paste0("trtmnt_", .x, recycle0 = T))
      ) %>% 
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      dplyr::select(plot,tree_id, tidyselect::starts_with("trtmnt_")) %>% 
      dplyr::group_by(plot,tree_id) %>% 
      dplyr::slice(1) %>% 
      dplyr::ungroup()
    , by = dplyr::join_by(plot,tree_id)
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    is_in_trtmnt_unit = ifelse(is.na(trtmnt_type) | trtmnt_type=="control",F,T)
    # , dplyr::across(c(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit),ordered)
  )

sure. let’s make a function to attach the canopy cover percentage to a plot with a given set of tree crown polygons

plot_crowns_cc_fn <- function(plots_sf, crowns_sf) {
  # plots idx
  plots_sf <- plots_sf %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      xxx_idx = dplyr::row_number()
      , xxx_area = sf::st_area(.) %>% as.numeric()
    )

  # map over plots to allow for plots that overlap to have their own answer
  plt_cc_temp <-
    plots_sf$xxx_idx %>%
    purrr::set_names() %>%
    purrr::map(
      \(x)
      crowns_sf %>%
        sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(plots_sf)) %>%
        sf::st_intersection(
          plots_sf %>%
            dplyr::filter(xxx_idx==x) %>%
            dplyr::select(xxx_idx,xxx_area)
        ) %>%
        dplyr::group_by(xxx_idx, xxx_area) %>%
        dplyr::summarise(
          geometry = sf::st_union(.)
          , .groups = "drop_last"
        ) %>%
        dplyr::ungroup() %>%
        dplyr::mutate(
          canopy_cov_area_m2 = sf::st_area(.) %>% as.numeric()
          , canopy_cov_pct = canopy_cov_area_m2/xxx_area
          , canopy_cov_geom = sf::st_geometry(.)
        ) %>%
        dplyr::select(-c(xxx_area)) %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry()
    ) %>%
    purrr::list_rbind()

  return(
    plots_sf %>%
      dplyr::left_join(plt_cc_temp, by = "xxx_idx") %>%
      dplyr::select(-c(xxx_idx, xxx_area))
  )
} 
# apply with the reference data

      sf::st_buffer(.$plot_radius_m)
    , crowns_sf = 
      validation_trees %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(crown_radius_m=crown_diam_m/2) %>% 
        sf::st_buffer(.$crown_radius_m)
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::rename_with(
    .cols = tidyselect::starts_with("canopy_")
    , ~ paste0("ref_",.x,recycle0 = T)
  )

4.4 Tree Detection Accuracy Overview

we’ll make a function that uses the following input data parameters to match predicted trees with validation/reference trees:

  • pred_data: predicted data point locations as sf data
  • ref_data: reference/validation/ground truth data point locations as sf data
  • max_dist_m: radius of search for matching
  • max_height_error_m: maximum allowable difference in height for to be considered correct match

for work in ponderosa pine forests, we generally set the max_dist_m to a 3 m radius to account for tree lean and slight horizontal misalignment in GPS data collection with 3 m representing the crown radius of a mature tree. we also typically set the max_height_error_m to 2 m for ponderosa pine evaluation but will need to reduce here to account for shorter trees

information used to inform the definition of “typical” crown width can be found in:

  • Gill et al. 2000
  • Bechtold 2003
  • Bechtold 2004
  • Purves et al. 2007

Then, we’ll aggregate the instance matching results to evaluate omission rate (false negative rate or miss rate), commission rate (false positive rate), precision, recall (detection rate), and the F-score metric. As a reminder, true positive (TP) instances correctly match ground truth instances with a prediction, commission predictions do not match a ground truth instance (false positive; FP), and omissions are ground truth instances for which no predictions match (false negative; FN)

\[\textrm{omission rate} = \frac{FN}{TP+FN}\]

\[\textrm{commission rate} = \frac{FP}{TP+FP}\]

\[\textrm{precision} = \frac{TP}{TP+FP}\]

\[\textrm{recall} = \frac{TP}{TP+FN}\]

\[ \textrm{F-score} = 2 \times \frac{\bigl(precision \times recall \bigr)}{\bigl(precision + recall \bigr)} \]

###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
# check df function
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
validate_df_fn <- function(data, required_cols = c("tree_height_m"), check_numeric = F) {
  # check data
  if(!inherits(data,"sf") && !inherits(data,"sfc")){stop("all input data requires POINT sf data")}
  if(
    !all( sf::st_is(data, c("POINT")) )
  ){
    stop("all input data requires POINT sf data")
  }
  # names
  # uses base::setdiff and base::names
  missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols, names(data))
  
  if(length(missing_cols) > 0){
    stop("all input data requires columns: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
  }
  
  # numeric
  if(check_numeric){
    non_numeric <- data %>%
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(required_cols)) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), ~ !is.numeric(.x))) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::everything()) %>%
      dplyr::filter(value == TRUE)

    if (nrow(non_numeric) > 0) {
      stop("columns must be numeric: ", paste(non_numeric$name, collapse = ", "))
    }
  }
  
  # is.na() catches both NA and NaN; is.infinite() catches Inf
  invalid_dta <- data %>%
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
    dplyr::summarise(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::all_of(required_cols)
        , ~ sum(is.na(.x) | is.infinite(.x))
      )
    ) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols = dplyr::everything()
      , names_to = "column"
      , values_to = "count"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(count > 0)

  if (nrow(invalid_dta) > 0) {
    bad_cols <- paste(invalid_dta$column, collapse = ", ")
    stop("invalid values (NA, NaN, or Inf) found in: ", bad_cols)
  }
  return(TRUE)
}
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
# match function
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
reference_prediction_match <- function(
  pred_data
  , ref_data
  , max_dist_m
  , max_height_error_m
) {
  #######################################################################
  # threshold checks
  #######################################################################
  if(
    any(is.na(max_dist_m)) || 
    any(is.null(max_dist_m)) || 
    !inherits(as.numeric(max_dist_m),"numeric")
  ){
    stop("`max_dist_m` must be numeric and not missing")
  }else{max_dist_m <- as.numeric(max_dist_m)[1]}
  if(
    any(is.na(max_height_error_m)) || 
    any(is.null(max_height_error_m)) || 
    !inherits(as.numeric(max_height_error_m),"numeric")
  ){
    stop("`max_height_error_m` must be numeric and not missing")
  }else{max_height_error_m <- as.numeric(max_height_error_m)[1]}
  #######################################################################
  # data checks
  #######################################################################
  if(nrow(pred_data)==0 | nrow(ref_data)==0){
    warning("no data so...?????")
    # return(NULL)
    
    if(nrow(pred_data)!=0){
      validate_df_fn(data = pred_data, required_cols = c("tree_height_m"), check_numeric = T)
      # sort to start with largest
      pred_data <- pred_data %>% 
        dplyr::arrange(desc(tree_height_m)) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(pred_match_idx = dplyr::row_number()) %>% 
        # add columns
        dplyr::mutate(
          ref_match_idx = as.numeric(NA)
          , pred_match_height_diff_m= as.numeric(NA)
          , pred_match_dist_m = as.numeric(NA)
          , ref_tree_height_m = as.numeric(NA)
        )
    }else{pred_data <- NULL}
    
    if(nrow(ref_data)!=0){
      validate_df_fn(data = ref_data, required_cols = c("tree_height_m"), check_numeric = T)
      # sort to start with largest
      ref_data <- ref_data %>% 
        dplyr::arrange(desc(tree_height_m)) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(ref_match_idx = dplyr::row_number()) %>% 
        # add columns
        dplyr::mutate(
          pred_match_idx = 0
          , pred_match_height_diff_m = as.numeric(NA)
          , pred_tree_height_m = as.numeric(NA)
          , pred_match_dist_m = as.numeric(NA)
        )
    }else{ref_data <- NULL}
    # return
    return(list(
      ref_data = ref_data
      , pred_data = pred_data
    ))
  }
  
  validate_df_fn(data = pred_data, required_cols = c("tree_height_m"), check_numeric = T)
  validate_df_fn(data = ref_data, required_cols = c("tree_height_m"), check_numeric = T)
  
  # proj
  if(!identical(
    sf::st_crs(pred_data, parameters = T)[["epsg"]]
    , sf::st_crs(ref_data, parameters = T)[["epsg"]]
  )){stop("data must have same projection. see `sf::st_crs()`")}
  # sort to start with largest
  pred_data <- pred_data %>% 
    dplyr::arrange(desc(tree_height_m)) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(pred_match_idx = dplyr::row_number())
  ref_data <- ref_data %>% 
    dplyr::arrange(desc(tree_height_m)) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(ref_match_idx = dplyr::row_number())
  #######################################################################
  # build a 2D kd-tree
  #######################################################################
    # Use the X and Y coordinates of the predicted to build the tree.
    pred_coords_temp <- 
      pred_data %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        X = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,1] %>% as.numeric()
        , Y = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,2] %>% as.numeric()
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::select(X,Y) %>% 
      sf::st_drop_geometry()
    # Use the X and Y coordinates of the reference to build the tree.
    ref_coords_temp <- 
      ref_data %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        X = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,1] %>% as.numeric()
        , Y = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,2] %>% as.numeric()
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::select(X,Y) %>% 
      sf::st_drop_geometry()
    
    # perform a fixed-radius search using RANN::nn2
    nn_ans_temp <- RANN::nn2(
      # the point cloud xy data (builds the kd-tree on this)
      data = pred_coords_temp
      # the seed point xy data (number of columns must be the same as data)
      , query = ref_coords_temp
      # maximum number of neighbors to find per query
      , k = min(nrow(pred_coords_temp),nrow(ref_coords_temp))
      # the search radius (rcyl)
      , radius = max_dist_m
      , searchtype = "radius"
    )
    # huh?
    # nn_ans_temp %>% class()
    # nn_ans_temp %>% names()
    # nn_ans_temp$nn.idx %>% nrow()
    # nrow(ref_coords_temp)
    # nn_ans_temp$nn.idx %>% ncol()
    # nrow(pred_coords_temp)
    # nn_ans_temp$nn.dists %>% nrow()
    # nrow(ref_coords_temp)
    # nn_ans_temp$nn.dists %>% ncol()
    # nrow(pred_coords_temp)
    # nn_ans_temp$nn.dists[1:11,] %>% dplyr::as_tibble() %>% dplyr::glimpse()
  #######################################################################  
  # iterate through the kd-tree to make matches
  #######################################################################
    if(nrow(ref_coords_temp)!=nrow(ref_data)){stop("bad kd-tree")}
    # add pred match tracker
    ref_data$pred_match_idx <- 0
    ref_data$pred_match_height_diff_m <- as.numeric(NA)
    ref_data$pred_tree_height_m <- as.numeric(NA)
    ref_data$pred_match_dist_m <- as.numeric(NA)
    for(i in 1:nrow(ref_coords_temp)){
      # get indices of points in the current cylinder (0 means no point found)
      nn_idx_pts <- nn_ans_temp$nn.idx[i, ]
      cyl_pts <- nn_idx_pts[nn_idx_pts > 0] 
      # remove already matched
      cyl_pts <- cyl_pts[!(cyl_pts %in% ref_data$pred_match_idx)] 
      # if available matches
      if(dplyr::coalesce(length(cyl_pts),0) >= 1) {
        # get heights
        # ref_data %>% dplyr::select(field_tree_id, tree_height_m) %>% dplyr::glimpse()
        # ref_data$tree_height_m[i]
        # pred_data$tree_height_m[cyl_pts]
        ht_diffs <- abs(ref_data$tree_height_m[i]-pred_data$tree_height_m[cyl_pts])
        # get the minimum value among elements below the threshold
        min_val <- min(ht_diffs[ht_diffs <= max_height_error_m], na.rm = T)
        # if not none within threshold
        if(!is.infinite(min_val)){
          # the index of that value in the original full vector
          cyl_idx <- which(ht_diffs == min_val)[1] # if multiple matches, takes the nearest
          match_idx <- cyl_pts[cyl_idx]
          # distance
          nn_dist_idx <- which(nn_idx_pts == match_idx)
          nn_dist <- nn_ans_temp$nn.dists[i,nn_dist_idx]
          # update match
          ref_data$pred_match_height_diff_m[i] <- min_val
          ref_data$pred_tree_height_m[i] <- pred_data$tree_height_m[match_idx]
          ref_data$pred_match_idx[i] <- match_idx
          ref_data$pred_match_dist_m[i] <- nn_dist
          
        }
      }
    }
  #######################################################################
  # add ref id to pred and return
  #######################################################################
  # pred_data %>% dplyr::glimpse()
  # ref_data %>% dplyr::glimpse()
  pred_data <- pred_data %>% 
    # get rid of columns we'll create
    dplyr::select( -dplyr::any_of(c(
      "hey_xxxxxxxxxx"
      , "pred_match_height_diff_m"
      , "pred_match_dist_m"
      , "ref_tree_height_m"
      , "ref_match_idx"
    ))) %>% 
    dplyr::left_join(
      ref_data %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::select(ref_match_idx, pred_match_idx, pred_match_height_diff_m, pred_match_dist_m, tree_height_m) %>% 
        dplyr::rename(ref_tree_height_m=tree_height_m)
      , by = "pred_match_idx"
    )
  return(list(
    ref_data = ref_data
    , pred_data = pred_data
  ))
}
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
# combine match to classify reference/predictions
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
ground_truth_prediction_match <- function(
  reference_prediction_match_ans
  , comp_cols = c("tree_height_m")
) {
  # check for missing both missing
  if(
    is.null(reference_prediction_match_ans$ref_data)
    && is.null(reference_prediction_match_ans$pred_data)
  ){
    warning("no data so...?????")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # if reference but no predictions...they are all omissions (FN)
  if(is.null(reference_prediction_match_ans$pred_data)){
    return_df <-
      reference_prediction_match_ans$ref_data %>%
      dplyr::filter(pred_match_idx==0 | is.na(pred_match_idx)) %>% 
      dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
        "ref_match_idx"
        , "pred_match_idx"
        , "pred_match_dist_m"
        # , "pred_tree_height_m"
        # , "tree_height_m"
        , comp_cols
      ))) %>% 
      dplyr::rename_with(
        .cols = dplyr::all_of(comp_cols)
        , .fn = ~paste0("ref_", .x, recycle0 = T)
      ) %>% 
      sf::st_set_geometry("ref_geometry") %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(match_grp = "omission")
    # make match_grp factor
    return_df <- return_df %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        match_grp = factor(
          match_grp
          , ordered = T
          , levels = c(
            "true positive"
            , "commission"
            , "omission"
          )
        ) %>% forcats::fct_rev()
      )
    return(return_df)
  }
  
  # if predictions but no reference...they are all commissions (FP)
  if(is.null(reference_prediction_match_ans$ref_data)){
    return_df <-
      reference_prediction_match_ans$pred_data %>%
      dplyr::filter(ref_match_idx==0 | is.na(ref_match_idx)) %>% 
      dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
        "ref_match_idx"
        , "pred_match_idx"
        , "pred_match_dist_m"
        # , "pred_tree_height_m"
        # , "tree_height_m"
        , comp_cols
      ))) %>% 
      dplyr::rename_with(
        .cols = dplyr::all_of(comp_cols)
        , .fn = ~paste0("pred_", .x, recycle0 = T)
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(pred_geometry = sf::st_geometry(.)) %>%
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(match_grp = "commission")
    # make match_grp factor
    return_df <- return_df %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        match_grp = factor(
          match_grp
          , ordered = T
          , levels = c(
            "true positive"
            , "commission"
            , "omission"
          )
        ) %>% forcats::fct_rev()
      )
    return(return_df)
  }
  
  ############# otherwise: nrow(ref_data)>0 & nrow(pred_data)>0
  ############# otherwise: nrow(ref_data)>0 & nrow(pred_data)>0
  ############# otherwise: nrow(ref_data)>0 & nrow(pred_data)>0
  ############# otherwise: nrow(ref_data)>0 & nrow(pred_data)>0
  ############# otherwise: nrow(ref_data)>0 & nrow(pred_data)>0
  # check for comparison cols
  comp_cols <- 
    comp_cols %>% 
    # remove whitespace
    stringr::str_trim() %>% 
    # keep only those with a value
    stringr::str_subset(".")
  if(inherits(comp_cols, "character") && length(comp_cols) > 0){
    validate_df_fn(data = reference_prediction_match_ans$ref_data, required_cols = comp_cols, check_numeric = T)
    validate_df_fn(data = reference_prediction_match_ans$pred_data, required_cols = comp_cols, check_numeric = T)
  }
  # tp matches
  return_df <-
    reference_prediction_match_ans$ref_data %>%
    dplyr::filter(pred_match_idx!=0 & !is.na(pred_match_idx)) %>% 
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
      "ref_match_idx"
      , "pred_match_idx"
      , "pred_match_dist_m"
      # , "pred_tree_height_m"
      # , "tree_height_m"
      , comp_cols
    ))) %>% 
    dplyr::rename_with(
      .cols = dplyr::all_of(comp_cols)
      , .fn = ~paste0("ref_", .x, recycle0 = T)
    ) %>% 
    sf::st_set_geometry("ref_geometry") %>% 
    # add on pred geom
    dplyr::inner_join(
      reference_prediction_match_ans$pred_data %>% 
        dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
          "ref_match_idx"
          , comp_cols
        ))) %>% 
        dplyr::rename_with(
          .cols = dplyr::all_of(comp_cols)
          , .fn = ~paste0("pred_", .x, recycle0 = T)
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(pred_geometry = sf::st_geometry(.)) %>%
        sf::st_drop_geometry()
      , by = "ref_match_idx"
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(match_grp = "true positive")
  
  # add omissions
  return_df <-
    return_df %>% 
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      reference_prediction_match_ans$ref_data %>%
        dplyr::filter(pred_match_idx==0 | is.na(pred_match_idx)) %>% 
        dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
          "ref_match_idx"
          , "pred_match_idx"
          , "pred_match_dist_m"
          # , "pred_tree_height_m"
          # , "tree_height_m"
          , comp_cols
        ))) %>% 
        dplyr::rename_with(
          .cols = dplyr::all_of(comp_cols)
          , .fn = ~paste0("ref_", .x, recycle0 = T)
        ) %>% 
        sf::st_set_geometry("ref_geometry") %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(match_grp = "omission")
    )
    
  # add commissions
  return_df <-
    return_df %>% 
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      reference_prediction_match_ans$pred_data %>%
        dplyr::filter(ref_match_idx==0 | is.na(ref_match_idx)) %>% 
        dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
          "ref_match_idx"
          , "pred_match_idx"
          , "pred_match_dist_m"
          # , "pred_tree_height_m"
          # , "tree_height_m"
          , comp_cols
        ))) %>% 
        dplyr::rename_with(
          .cols = dplyr::all_of(comp_cols)
          , .fn = ~paste0("pred_", .x, recycle0 = T)
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(pred_geometry = sf::st_geometry(.)) %>%
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(match_grp = "commission")
    )
  
  # make match_grp factor
  return_df <- return_df %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      match_grp = factor(
        match_grp
        , ordered = T
        , levels = c(
          "true positive"
          , "commission"
          , "omission"
        )
      ) %>% forcats::fct_rev()
    )
  
  
  if(inherits(comp_cols, "character") && length(comp_cols) > 0){
    # add a tiny value (eps) to the denominator for pct_diff_ 
    # calcs to prevent division by zero...where pct_diff_ is used for MAPE summary
    eps <- 1e-5
    return_df <- 
      return_df %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        # 'diff_' columns are calculated as the predicted value minus the actual value
        dplyr::across(
          .cols = paste0(
            "ref_"
            , comp_cols # c("tree_height_m", "dbh_cm")
            , recycle0 = T
          )
          , .fns = ~ base::get(stringr::str_replace(dplyr::cur_column(), "^ref_", "pred_")) - .x
          , .names = "diff_{stringr::str_remove(.col, '^ref_')}"
        )
        # 'pct_diff_' columns are calculated as the actual value minus the predicted value divided by the actual value
        , dplyr::across(
          .cols = paste0(
            "ref_"
            , comp_cols # c("tree_height_m", "dbh_cm")
            , recycle0 = T
          )
          # 
          , .fns = ~ (.x-base::get(stringr::str_replace(dplyr::cur_column(), "^ref_", "pred_")))/(.x + eps)
          , .names = "pct_diff_{stringr::str_remove(.col, '^ref_')}"
        )
      ) 
  }
  # return
  if(nrow(return_df)==0){
    warning("no records found for ground truth to predition matching")
    return(NULL)
  }else{
    return(return_df)
  }
  
}

take that thing for a spin for a single plot.

To account for tree lean and potential slight spatial misalignment between the UAS point clouds and the ground-based field coordinates along the unit boundary, UAS-predicted trees located outside the boundary but within half the horizontal matching threshold were permitted to qualify as true positives, though unmatched exterior trees were excluded from false positive counts.

reference_prediction_match_ans_temp <- reference_prediction_match(
  pred_data = 
    treetops_sf %>% 
      dplyr::filter(
        tree_height_m>=min_tree_ht_m
        , dplyr::coalesce(inrange_th_votes,0)<=max_inrange_th_votes
      ) %>% 
      sf::st_intersection(
        validation_plots %>% 
          dplyr::slice(33) %>% 
          dplyr::mutate(plot_radius_m = plot_radius_m+1) %>% # 1 = 0.5*max_dist_m where max_dist_m=allowable search distance for TP match
          sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(treetops_sf)) %>% 
          sf::st_buffer(.$plot_radius_m) %>% 
          dplyr::select(plot_area_m2)
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::left_join(
        treetops_sf %>% 
          # clip to study boundary
          sf::st_intersection(
            validation_plots %>% 
              dplyr::slice(33) %>% 
              sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(treetops_sf)) %>% 
              sf::st_buffer(.$plot_radius_m) %>% 
              dplyr::mutate(is_in_stand = T)
          ) %>% 
          sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
          dplyr::select(treeID, is_in_stand)
        , by = "treeID"
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        is_in_stand = dplyr::coalesce(is_in_stand,F)
      )
  , ref_data = 
    validation_trees %>% 
      dplyr::inner_join(
        validation_plots %>% dplyr::slice(33) %>% sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% dplyr::select(plot)
        , by = "plot"
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::rename(tree_height_m=height_m, dbh_cm=dbh_cm, tree_cbh_m=cbh_m) %>% 
      sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(treetops_sf))
  , max_dist_m = 2 # round(median(validation_trees$crown_width_m)/2)
  , max_height_error_m = 1.5 # round(sd(validation_trees$height_m)*1.1,1)
)

# reference_prediction_match_ans_temp$pred_data %>% dplyr::glimpse()

the ground_truth_prediction_match() uses the output from reference_prediction_match() and creates a nice, clean data frame with the instances classified as TP, FP, or FN for use in aggregating to calculate detection accuracy metrics. Optionally, users can set the foundation for individual tree physical measurement accuracy assessment via the comp_cols argument (see the diff_* and pct_diff_* columns in the output)

gt_temp <- ground_truth_prediction_match(
  reference_prediction_match_ans = reference_prediction_match_ans_temp
  , comp_cols = c("tree_height_m", "dbh_cm", "tree_cbh_m")
)

4.4.1 Example: Detection Accuracy

let’s make a function to calculate the detection accuracy metrics based on aggregated TP, FP, and FN counts

###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
# first function takes df with cols tp_n, fp_n, and fn_n to calculate rates
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
confusion_matrix_scores_fn <- function(df) {
  df %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    omission_rate = dplyr::case_when(
      dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fn_n,0) == 0 ~ 0 # if there are no actual trees, there is nothing to miss
      , dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fn_n,0) > 0 ~ 1 # every single actual tree was missed
      , dplyr::coalesce(fn_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) > 0 ~ 0
      , T ~ fn_n/(tp_n+fn_n)
    ) # False Negative Rate or Miss Rate
    , commission_rate = dplyr::case_when(
      dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fp_n,0) == 0 ~ 0 # if no predictions are made, the model could not have made any commission errors
      , dplyr::coalesce(fp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) > 0 ~ 0
      , T ~ fp_n/(tp_n+fp_n)
    ) # False Positive Rate
    , precision = dplyr::case_when(
      dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fp_n,0) == 0 ~ 1 # if no predictions are made, the model made zero incorrect positive claims
      , dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fp_n,0) > 0 ~ 0
      , T ~ tp_n/(tp_n+fp_n)
    )
    , recall = dplyr::case_when(
      dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fn_n,0) == 0 ~ 1 # if there are no actual trees, there is nothing to miss
      , dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fn_n,0) > 0 ~ 0 # every single actual tree was missed
      , T ~ tp_n/(tp_n+fn_n)
    )
    , f_score = dplyr::case_when(
      dplyr::coalesce(precision,0) == 0 | dplyr::coalesce(recall,0) == 0 ~ 0
      , T ~ 2 * ( (precision*recall)/(precision+recall) )
    )    
  ) 
}
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
# aggregate results from ground_truth_prediction_match()
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
agg_ground_truth_match <- function(ground_truth_prediction_match_ans) {
  if(nrow(ground_truth_prediction_match_ans)==0){return(NULL)}
  if( !(names(ground_truth_prediction_match_ans) %>% stringr::str_equal("match_grp") %>% any()) ){stop("ground_truth_prediction_match_ans must contain `match_grp` column")}
  
  # check for difference columns (contains "_diff") and calc rmse for only those to return a single line df with colums for each diff_rmse
    if(
      (ground_truth_prediction_match_ans %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::select(tidyselect::starts_with("diff_") | tidyselect::starts_with("pct_diff_")) %>% 
        ncol() )>0
    ){
      # get rmse and mean difference/error for all columns with "_diff" but not "pct_diff"
      # get mape for all columns with "pct_diff" but not "diff_"
      rmse_df <- 
        ground_truth_prediction_match_ans %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
        dplyr::select(
          tidyselect::starts_with("diff_")
          | tidyselect::starts_with("pct_diff_")
        ) %>%
        tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::everything(), values_drop_na = T) %>% 
        dplyr::group_by(name) %>% 
        dplyr::summarise(
          sq = sum(value^2, na.rm = T)
          , mean = mean(value, na.rm = T)
          , sumabs = sum(abs(value), na.rm = T)
          , nomiss = sum(!is.na(value))
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(
          rmse = dplyr::case_when(
            dplyr::coalesce(nomiss,0)==0 ~ as.numeric(NA)
            , T ~ sqrt(sq/nomiss)
          )
          , mape = dplyr::case_when(
            dplyr::coalesce(nomiss,0)==0 ~ as.numeric(NA)
            , T ~ sumabs/nomiss
          )
        ) %>% 
        # NA nonsense values
        dplyr::mutate(
          mape = dplyr::case_when(
            stringr::str_starts(name, "pct_diff_") ~ mape
            , T ~ as.numeric(NA)
          )
          , rmse = dplyr::case_when(
            stringr::str_starts(name, "pct_diff_") ~ as.numeric(NA)
            , T ~ rmse
          )
          , mean = dplyr::case_when(
            stringr::str_starts(name, "pct_diff_") ~ as.numeric(NA)
            , T ~ mean
          )
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::select(name,rmse,mean,mape) %>% 
        tidyr::pivot_wider(
          names_from = name
          , values_from = c(rmse,mean,mape)
          , names_glue = "{name}_{.value}"
        ) %>% 
        # remove columns with NA in all rows
        dplyr::select( dplyr::where( ~!all(is.na(.x)) ) )
      
      if(
        dplyr::coalesce(nrow(rmse_df),0)==0
        || dplyr::coalesce(ncol(rmse_df),0)==0
      ){
        # empty df
        rmse_df <- dplyr::tibble()
      }
    }else{
      # empty df
      rmse_df <- dplyr::tibble()
    }
  
  # count by match group
    agg <-
      ground_truth_prediction_match_ans %>% 
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
      dplyr::count(match_grp) %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        match_grp = dplyr::recode_values(
          match_grp
          , "true positive"~"tp"
          , "commission"~"fp"
          , "omission"~"fn"
        )
      )
    # true positive, false positive, false negative rates
    return_df <- dplyr::tibble(match_grp = c("tp","fp","fn")) %>% 
      dplyr::left_join(agg, by = "match_grp") %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(.cols = c(n), .fn = ~dplyr::coalesce(.x,0))) %>% 
      tidyr::pivot_wider(
        names_from = match_grp
        , values_from = c(n)
        , names_glue = "{match_grp}_{.value}"
      )
    # rates, precision, recall, f-score
    return_df <- confusion_matrix_scores_fn(return_df)
    # add rmse
    if(nrow(rmse_df)>0){
      return_df <- return_df %>% dplyr::bind_cols(rmse_df)
    }
  # return
  return(return_df)
}

4.5 Tree-level Physical Measurement Accuracy Overview

Physical measurement accuracy metrics such as RMSE, MAPE, and Mean Error of individual tree form measurements (e.g. height, diameter) are calculated by aggregating the differences between the estimated tree attributes and the field reference values for instances classified as True Positives. These metrics tell us about the method’s ability to accurately quantify the form of the trees it successfully identified.

to prepare our results for analysis, we will develop a function that aggregates the tree-level data into a single record for each metric-error measurement combination. this function will calculate detection performance metrics such as F-score, precision, and recall (using the confusion_matrix_scores_fn() we defined above), as well as individual tree physical measurement accuracy metrics including Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Error (ME), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) to assess the accuracy of our tree form measurements. this could be a valuable function for any future analysis comparing predictions to reference data.

here are the individual tree physical measurement accuracy metric formulas:

\[ \textrm{RMSE} = \sqrt{ \frac{ \sum_{i=1}^{N} (y_{i} - \hat{y_{i}})^{2}}{N}} \]

\[ \textrm{ME} = \frac{ \sum_{i=1}^{N} (\hat{y_{i}} - y_{i})}{N} \]

\[ \textrm{MAPE} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} \left| \frac{y_{i} - \hat{y_{i}}}{y_{i}} \right| \]

Where \(N\) is equal to the total number of correctly matched trees, \(y_i\) is the ground truth measured value and \(\hat{y_i}\) is the predicted value of \(i\)

There is a lot going on in our agg_ground_truth_match() function but it’s application is straightforward enough:

  • The minimum required input is a data frame of the raw instance matches with a column named match_grp which is string/factor with the levels “true positive”, “commission”, and “omission” as returned by the ground_truth_prediction_match() function
  • Optionally, if the data contain columns with the prefix “diff_” the mean error (ME) is calculated for those columns with the return having the suffix “_mean” and the RMSE is calculated for those columns with the return having the suffix “_rmse”
    • interpretation of the ME is enhanced if these “diff_” columns are calculated as the predicted value minus the actual value (e.g. pred_diameter_m - gt_diameter_m)
  • Optionally, if the data contain columns with the prefix “pct_diff_” the mean absolute percent error (MAPE) is calculated for those columns with the return having the suffix “_mape”
    • these “pct_diff_” columns are calculated as the actual value minus the predicted value divided by the actual value (e.g. (gt_diameter_m - pred_diameter_m)/gt_diameter_m)

4.6 Implement Accuracy Evaluation

because we have plot-level reference field data but a complete census of predictions, we need to perform accuracy evaluation for each plot and then aggregate to the entire study site.

let’s perform instance matching for each plot and then bring those results together after

4.7 Tree Detection Accuracy Results

Here we’ll perform individual tree detection (ITD) performance evaluation of the UAS method to verify the it’s ability to segment individual trees. Our instance matching method pairs field-mapped trees to UAS-detected trees to calculate:

  • Recall - the proportion of real field trees successfully detected by the UAS (or the inverse of omission errors)
  • Precision - the proportion of UAS-detected trees that correspond to real trees (or the inverse of commission errors)
  • F-score - the harmonic mean between recall and precsion representing balanced detection accuracy

Combining individual-level tree detection metrics with plot-level canopy and height aggregates will establish the statistical confidence we need to scale the UAS spatial tree list data across the entire study area to evaluate treatment effects on residual spatial structure. This focus aligns with contemporary management in pinyon-juniper systems, which prioritizes horizontal canopy architecture, clump configuration, and treeless open gaps as ecologically meaningful indicators of ecosystem health and fuel-hazard risk across these arid landscapes.

interesting to see the variation in detection accuracy across the different treatment types. the more aggressive treatments (i.e. treatments that removed more trees and left fewer residual trees) have a smaller margin for error with respect to tree detection accuracy since each tree carries more weight. however, the more open stand conditions created by the more aggressive treatments should make it easier to detect each individual if they are spaced with openings between individuals. at the same time the units with a high proportion of slash piles might result in increased commission rate (i.e. higher number of false positive tree predictions) even though we applied a slash pile mask. an additional data check may be needed for the remaining trees to check whether or not they are “green” and perhaps we should increase our strictness for what we spectrally include as a non-dead tree to match the field data collection method of only measuring live trees

let’s see the relationship between tree detection (recall rate) and tree height. we’ll look at true positive and omissions (FN) and use the field-measured tree height to quantify the proportion of trees within a height bin that were detected by the UAS method

# make ggplot2::cut_* bins pretty
make_bins_pretty <- function(bin_factor, suffix = "") {
  # convert factor to character and remove brackets and parens
  clean_labels <- bin_factor %>%
    as.character() %>%
    stringr::str_replace_all(c("\\[" = "", "\\(" = "", "\\]" = "", "\\)" = "")) %>%
    stringr::str_replace(",", "-")
  
  # suffix
  if(stringr::str_squish(suffix) != "" && inherits(suffix,"character")){
    clean_labels <- stringr::str_c(clean_labels, " ", suffix) %>% stringr::str_squish()
  }
  
  # reorder based on the original factor levels 
  forcats::fct_reorder(factor(clean_labels), as.numeric(bin_factor))
}

#   levels()

parse_cut_levels <- function(l) {
  
  cut_points <- 
    stringr::str_remove_all(l, "[\\[\\]() ]") %>% 
    stringr::str_split_fixed(",", 2) %>% 
    as.numeric() %>% 
    unique() %>% 
    sort()
  
  final_breaks <- cut_points
  final_breaks[1] <- 0
  final_breaks[length(cut_points)] <- Inf
  # final_breaks <- c(0, cut_points, Inf)
  
  return(sort(unique(final_breaks)))
}

the commission error (percentage shown in the gray bar) is highest for the small trees which suggests we could potentially improve our ITD window function to decrease the number of trees detected in this height range. However, going back to the detection rate above, this same height range also had the lowest detection rate which would suggest we increase the number of trees identified in this height range. This conflict suggests that the trees in this height range are likely difficult to detect for the study area using the data and ITD methods used in this study. For example, they may be subordinate to directly adjacent taller trees with the crowns interlocking, so they are often grouped with the taller tree during the CHM-based ITD.

dta_temp <-
  ground_truth_prediction_match_ans %>% 
  dplyr::filter(match_grp=="true positive") %>% 
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  dplyr::bind_rows() %>% 
  dplyr::bind_cols(

# plt fn temp
plt_scatter_fn <- function(
    dta
    , which_col = "crown_diameter_m"
    , title_lab = "Crown Diameter"
    , x_lab = "reference crown diam. (m)" # latex2exp::TeX("reference area ($m^2$)")
    , y_lab = "predicted crown diam. (m)" # latex2exp::TeX("predicted area ($m^2$)")
){
    d <- dta
    # construct the formula: "y_var ~ x_var"
    y_var <- paste0("pred_",which_col)
    x_var <- paste0("ref_",which_col)
    formula_obj <- stats::as.formula(
      paste( 
        y_var
        , "~"
        , x_var 
      )
    )
    lm_temp <- lm(
      formula = formula_obj
      , data = d
    )
    # summary(lm_temp)
    # scales::percent(summary(lm_temp)$r.squared, accuracy = 0.1)
    lmf_temp <- paste0(
      "y = "
      , scales::number(summary(lm_temp)$coefficients[2,1], accuracy = 0.01) #slope
      , "x"
      , ifelse(summary(lm_temp)$coefficients[1,1]<0," - ", " + ")
      , scales::number(abs(summary(lm_temp)$coefficients[1,1]), accuracy = 0.01) #intercept
    )
    # scale limits
    max_val <- max( 
      max(d[[y_var]],na.rm=T)
      , max(d[[x_var]],na.rm=T)
    )
    
    # annotations
    if( any( stringr::str_equal(names(d), paste0("diff_",which_col, "_rmse")) ) ){
    rmse_val <- d %>% 
      dplyr::slice(1) %>% 
      dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(paste0("diff_",which_col, "_rmse"))) %>% 
      dplyr::pull(1) %>% 
      unique()
      rmse_val <- dplyr::case_when(
        stringr::str_ends(which_col,"_cm") ~ scales::number(rmse_val, accuracy = 0.1, suffix = " (cm)")
        , stringr::str_ends(which_col,"_m") ~ scales::number(rmse_val, accuracy = 0.01, suffix = " (m)")
        , stringr::str_ends(which_col,"_m2") ~ scales::number(rmse_val, accuracy = 0.1, suffix = " (m²)")
        , stringr::str_ends(which_col,"_pct") ~ scales::percent(rmse_val, accuracy = 0.1)
        , T ~ scales::number(rmse_val, accuracy = 0.1)
      )
    }else{rmse_val <- NA}
    if( any( stringr::str_equal(names(d), paste0("pct_diff_",which_col, "_mape")) ) ){
      mape_val <- d %>% 
        dplyr::slice(1) %>% 
        dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(paste0("pct_diff_",which_col, "_mape"))) %>% 
        dplyr::pull(1) %>% 
        unique() %>% 
        scales::percent(accuracy = 0.1)
    }else{mape_val <- NA}
    if( any( stringr::str_equal(names(d), paste0("diff_",which_col, "_mean")) ) ){
      me_val <- d %>% 
        dplyr::slice(1) %>% 
        dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(paste0("diff_",which_col, "_mean"))) %>% 
        dplyr::pull(1) %>% 
        unique()
        me_val <- dplyr::case_when(
          stringr::str_ends(which_col,"_cm") ~ scales::number(me_val, accuracy = 0.1, suffix = " (cm)")
          , stringr::str_ends(which_col,"_m") ~ scales::number(me_val, accuracy = 0.01, suffix = " (m)")
          , stringr::str_ends(which_col,"_m2") ~ scales::number(me_val, accuracy = 0.1, suffix = " (m²)")
          , stringr::str_ends(which_col,"_pct") ~ scales::percent(me_val, accuracy = 0.1)
          , T ~ scales::number(me_val, accuracy = 0.1)
        )
    }else{me_val <- NA}
    
    # plot
    p <- d %>% 
      ggplot2::ggplot(mapping = ggplot2::aes(y = .data[[y_var]], x = .data[[x_var]])) +
      ggplot2::geom_abline(color = "gray33", lwd = 1) +
      ggplot2::geom_point(color = "brown", alpha = 0.7, size = 0.9) +
      ggplot2::geom_smooth(lwd = 0.8, method = "lm", se=F, color = "gray", linetype = "dashed") +
      ggplot2::annotate(
        "text", 
        x = -Inf, y = Inf # Top Left
        , label = 
          # paste0(
          #   "R^2 == "
          #   , scales::number((summary(lm_temp)$r.squared)*100, accuracy = 0.1)
          #   , "*'%'"
          # )
          paste0(
            "RMSE = ", rmse_val
            , ifelse(!is.na(mape_val), paste0("\nMAPE = ", mape_val),"")
            , ifelse(!is.na(me_val), paste0("\nME = ", me_val),"")
            , "\n"
            , lmf_temp
            , "\n R² = "
            # , scales::number((summary(lm_temp)$r.squared)*100, accuracy = 0.1, suffix = "%")
            , scales::number((summary(lm_temp)$r.squared), accuracy = 0.01)
          )
        , hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.1
        , parse = F
        , size = 3
      ) +
      # ggplot2::facet_wrap(
      #   facets = dplyr::vars(dataset_factor), scales = "free", axis.labels = "all"
      #   # , labeller = ggplot2::labeller(class = ggplot2::label_wrap_gen(width = 10))
      # ) +
      ggplot2::labs(
        x = x_lab
        , y = y_lab
        # , color = "image-field\ndiameter diff."
        # , subtitle = latex2exp::TeX("bulk volume ($m^3$) comparison")
        # , subtitle = paste("Predicted", title_lab,"versus Reference", title_lab)
      ) +
      ggplot2::theme_light() +
      ggplot2::theme(
        strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", color = "black")
      ) 
    if(stringr::str_ends(which_col,"_pct")){
      p + 
        ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, max_val ), labels = scales::percent, expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0,0.1))) +
        ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max_val ), labels = scales::percent, expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0,0.1)))
    }else{
      return(
        p + 
        ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, max_val ), expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0,0.1))) +
        ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max_val ), expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0,0.1)))
      )
    }
  }

let’s shift our focus to relative error (MAPE) while providing absolute context (RMSE and ME) as text or secondary metrics to look into the penalty we face due to inaccuracies in DBH for small stems. for example, a 3 cm error on a 6 cm small tree is a 50% relative error while that same 3 cm error on a 30 cm merchantable tree is a minor 10% error.

let’s look into the crown diameter prediction error over the range of tree sizes and use LOESS smoothing to highlight the trend in relative prediction error

4.9 Plot-Level Accuracy Results

In this section, we’ll shift our focus from individual trees to plot-level predictions by aggregating tree-level UAS predictions and field-reference values irrespective of individual instance matches. Evaluating aggregated, plot-level forest inventory metrics helps us understand how accurately the UAS data captures broader forest structural metrics like canopy cover.

Since the circular ground-based field plots are relatively small with a 10.0 m radius and 314.2 m² area, the plot-level field data is insufficient to directly quantify macro-spatial patterns like tree clump sizes and treeless opening gaps. Our objective is to use the complete-coverage UAS data to map these broad-scale spatial patterns across the entire study area. However, validating UAS-derived spatial patterns against small field plots introduces several scaling and alignment challenges. The constraints of small field plots amplify compounding measurement errors, including boundary edge effects that complicate whether a tree is “in” or “out” of the plot, minor GPS misalignments between ground-based positions and the UAS, and the notorious difficulty of measuring two-dimensional crown dimensions in the field.

To overcome these fine-scale spatial discrepancies, we’ll focus our UAS evaluation on plot-level aggregate metrics that naturally smooth out localized spatial noise while still capturing the broad-scale forest structure required for our UAS validation objectives. We’ll use plot-level canopy cover as the primary horizontal metric because it directly captures canopy openness and tree cover without being heavily influenced by minor stem-mapping misalignments. To complement this horizontal dimension, we’ll evaluate mean tree height at the plot level to validate the vertical profile representation of the UAS data. We’ll calculate these plot-level metrics by aggregating tree-level UAS predictions and field-reference values irrespective of individual instance matching. Following the terminology established by Li (2009), plot tree height is defined as the average height of individual trees within a plot boundary. While Li (2009) used a diameter threshold of at least 5 inches DBH to calcuate plot tree height, we used a tree height threshold of 2 m applied to both the UAS and field trees. For both canopy cover and plot tree height, we’ll calculate Mean Error (ME) to quantify systematic over- or under-estimation (bias) and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) to measure total prediction variance.

We’ll assess UAS prediction accuracy at two spatial scales:

  1. Overall Study Site: Aggregating data across all field-measured plots to evaluate site-wide performance.
  2. Treatment Level: Aggregating data within the field-measured plots associated with each specific treatment, including the control units.

Combining plot-level tree crown and height aggregations with individual-level tree detection metrics will establish the statistical confidence we need to scale the UAS spatial tree list data across the entire study area to evaluate treatment effects on residual spatial structure. This focus aligns with contemporary management paradigms in pinyon-juniper systems, which prioritize horizontal canopy architecture, clump configuration, and interspace connectivity as ecologically meaningful indicators of ecosystem health and fuel-hazard risk across arid landscapes.

4.9.1 Canopy Cover Evaluation

We’ll start by evaluating UAS-predicted canopy cover compared to field-measured values. Recall that to obtain field-measured canopy cover, we averaged the field-recorded horizontal crown length and width to approximate a circular diameter, used that diameter to calculate a 2D circular crown area for each tree, and determined the proportion of each plot covered by these assumed circular crowns. For each plot, we’ll compare this proportion to the canopy cover predicted by the UAS using trees whose tree-top points fall within the plot boundaries irrespective of if a tree was matched as a true positive in our instance matching evaluation. Requiring the tree-top point to fall within the plot mimics the field technique of only measuring stems located inside the plot boundaries. The main caveats attached to this canopy cover accuracy evaluation are that measuring crown dimensions accurately using manual ground techniques is notoriously difficult, and the simple circular shape assumption rarely matches the irregular crown morphologies found in the real-world (Rautiainen et al. 2008; Gallardo-Salazar & Pompa-García 2020; Ren et al. 2024).

############################################################################
# function to get nearest neighbor distance given a set of points
############################################################################
get_nn_point_dist <- function(df_w_xy){
  if(nrow(df_w_xy) < 2){
    return(
      df_w_xy %>% 
        dplyr::select(-c(X,Y)) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(nn_dist_m=as.numeric(NA))
    )
  }
  # perform a fixed-radius search using RANN::nn2
  # ?RANN::nn2
  nn_ans_temp <- RANN::nn2(
    # the point cloud xy data (builds the kd-tree on this)
    data = df_w_xy %>% sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% dplyr::select(X,Y)
    # maximum number of neighbors to find per query
    , k = nrow(df_w_xy)
    , searchtype = "standard"
  )
  # nn_ans_temp
  # nn_ans_temp$nn.dists[,1] # first col is self-dist which should be 0
  # nn_ans_temp$nn.dists[,2] # second col is nearest non-self dist
  
  ret_df <- df_w_xy %>% 
    dplyr::select(-c(X,Y)) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      nn_dist_m = nn_ans_temp$nn.dists[,2]
    )
    # # dplyr::glimpse(ret_df)
    # ggplot2::ggplot(data=ret_df) + 
    #   ggplot2::geom_sf(mapping=ggplot2::aes(color = factor(round(nn_dist_m,3)))) +
    #   ggplot2::scale_color_viridis_d(option="cividis")
  return(ret_df)
}

validation_plots_polygons <-
  plot_crowns_cc_fn(
    plots_sf = validation_plots_polygons
    , crowns_sf = pred_crowns_temp
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::rename_with(
    .cols = tidyselect::starts_with("canopy_")
    , ~ paste0("pred_",.x,recycle0 = T)
  ) %>% 
  # add tree counts based on tree top point intersection with plot
  dplyr::rename_with(
    .cols = c("n_trees","trees_per_ha")
    , ~ paste0("ref_",.x,recycle0 = T)
  ) %>% 
  # add pred tree count and nn dist and mean stand height
  dplyr::left_join(
    pred_trees_in_validation_plots_w_dups %>% 
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
      dplyr::group_by(plot) %>% 
      dplyr::summarize(
        n_trees = dplyr::n()
        , median_nn_dist_m = median(nn_dist_m,na.rm=T)
        , mean_nn_dist_m = mean(nn_dist_m,na.rm=T)
        , mean_tree_height_m = mean(tree_height_m,na.rm=T)
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
      dplyr::rename_with(
        .cols = -c(plot)
        , ~ paste0("pred_",.x,recycle0 = T)
      )
    , by = "plot"
  ) %>% 
  # add ref nn dist and mean stand height
  dplyr::left_join(
    validation_trees %>% 
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
      dplyr::group_by(plot) %>% 
      dplyr::summarize(
        median_nn_dist_m = median(nn_dist_m,na.rm=T)
        , mean_nn_dist_m = mean(nn_dist_m,na.rm=T)
        , mean_tree_height_m = mean(height_m,na.rm=T)
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
      dplyr::rename_with(
        .cols = -c(plot)
        , ~ paste0("ref_",.x,recycle0 = T)
      )
    , by = "plot"
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    pred_n_trees = dplyr::coalesce(pred_n_trees,0)
    , pred_canopy_cov_pct = dplyr::coalesce(pred_canopy_cov_pct,0)
    , pred_canopy_cov_area_m2 = dplyr::coalesce(pred_canopy_cov_area_m2,0)
    , pred_trees_per_ha = pred_n_trees/(plot_area_m2/10000)
    , diff_canopy_cov_pct = pred_canopy_cov_pct-ref_canopy_cov_pct
    , diff_trees_per_ha = pred_trees_per_ha-ref_trees_per_ha
    , diff_median_nn_dist_m = pred_median_nn_dist_m-ref_median_nn_dist_m
    , diff_mean_nn_dist_m = pred_mean_nn_dist_m-ref_mean_nn_dist_m
    , diff_mean_tree_height_m = pred_mean_tree_height_m-ref_mean_tree_height_m
  )

let’s check the relationship between the UAS and reference field plot-level canopy cover measurements

# function to get aggregate accuracy metrics
get_me_rmse_fn <- function(df_w_diffs) {

  if(nrow(df_w_diffs)==0){return(NULL)}
  
  # check for difference columns (contains "_diff") and calc rmse for only those to return a single line df with colums for each diff_rmse
  diffs_nms <- df_w_diffs %>% 
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
    dplyr::select(tidyselect::starts_with("diff_")) %>% 
    names() %>% 
    stringr::str_subset(pattern="^diff_")
  
  if(length(diffs_nms)==0){return(NULL)}
  
  # check for reference so that rrmse can be done
  ref_nms <- diffs_nms %>% stringr::str_replace("^diff_", "ref_")
  yes_ref_nms <- 
    df_w_diffs %>% 
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
    dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(ref_nms)) %>% 
    names()
  
  # setdiff(ref_nms,yes_ref_nms)
  
  if(
    length(setdiff(ref_nms,yes_ref_nms))>0
  ){
    stop(paste("missing", paste0(setdiff(ref_nms,yes_ref_nms), collapse = ","), "columns which are required for RRMSE" ))
  }
  
  # check for reference so that rrmse can be done
  pred_nms <- diffs_nms %>% stringr::str_replace("^diff_", "pred_")
  yes_pred_nms <- 
    df_w_diffs %>% 
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
    dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(pred_nms)) %>% 
    names()
  
  # setdiff(pred_nms,yes_pred_nms)
  
  if(
    length(setdiff(pred_nms,yes_pred_nms))>0
  ){
    stop(paste("missing", paste0(setdiff(pred_nms,yes_pred_nms), collapse = ","), "columns which are required for RRMSE" ))
  }
  # get rmse and mean difference/error for all columns with "_diff" but not "pct_diff"
  # get mape for all columns with "pct_diff" but not "diff_"
  rmse_df <- 
    1:length(diffs_nms) %>% 
    # this is all so that data can be grouped when it comes into the function
    purrr::map(function(var_nm_idx){
      df_w_diffs %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(
          dplyr::across(
            .cols = diffs_nms[var_nm_idx]
            , .fns = ~.x
            , .names = "xxxdiff"
          )
          , dplyr::across(
            .cols = ref_nms[var_nm_idx]
            , .fns = ~.x
            , .names = "xxxref"
          )
          , dplyr::across(
            .cols = pred_nms[var_nm_idx]
            , .fns = ~.x
            , .names = "xxxpred"
          )
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::summarise(
          sq_diff = sum(xxxdiff^2, na.rm = T)
          , mean_diff = mean(xxxdiff, na.rm = T)
          , mape = mean( abs(xxxdiff / ifelse(xxxref==0,xxxref+1e-10,xxxref)), na.rm=T )
          , nomiss_diff = sum(!is.na(xxxdiff))
          , mean_ref = mean(xxxref, na.rm = T)
          , mean_pred = mean(xxxpred, na.rm = T)
          , nomiss_ref = sum(!is.na(xxxref))
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(
          rmse = dplyr::case_when(
            dplyr::coalesce(nomiss_diff,0)==0 ~ as.numeric(NA)
            , T ~ sqrt(sq_diff/nomiss_diff)
          )
          , rrmse = dplyr::case_when(
            dplyr::coalesce(nomiss_ref,0)==0 ~ as.numeric(NA)
            , mean_ref==0 ~ rmse/(mean_ref+1e-10)
            , T ~ rmse/mean_ref
          )
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::rename(mean=mean_diff) %>% 
        # dplyr::select(-c(sq_diff,nomiss_diff,mean_ref,nomiss_ref)) %>% 
        dplyr::select(rmse,rrmse,mean,mape,mean_ref,mean_pred) %>% 
        dplyr::rename_with(
          .cols = c(rmse,rrmse,mean,mape)
          , ~ paste0(diffs_nms[var_nm_idx],"_",.x)
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::rename_with(
          .cols = c(mean_pred)
          , ~ paste0("mean_",pred_nms[var_nm_idx])
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::rename_with(
          .cols = c(mean_ref)
          , ~ paste0("mean_",ref_nms[var_nm_idx])
        )
    }) %>% 
    purrr::list_cbind()
  # rmse_df %>% dplyr::glimpse()
  # add back on grouping levels if data was grouped
  return_df <- 
    df_w_diffs %>% 
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
    dplyr::count() %>% 
    dplyr::rename(n_obs_for_error_metrics = n)
    
      
    if(
      dplyr::coalesce(nrow(rmse_df),0)==0
      || dplyr::coalesce(ncol(rmse_df),0)==0
    ){
      # empty df
      rmse_df <- dplyr::tibble()
    }
  # return
  return(return_df %>% dplyr::bind_cols(rmse_df))
}

The plot-level aggregation comparing the canopy cover of the field method to the UAS method yielded an RMSE of 7.8% and a mean error (ME) of 3.6%. These values mean that the average UAS prediction of plot-level canopy cover is off by about ±7.8 percentage points from the field-measured value which is generally considered highly accurate and operationally acceptable. The positive ME of 3.6% means that, on average across all plots, the UAS method is systematically overpredicting canopy cover by 3.6 percentage points compared to the field data.
